jira_comment:
Verdict: inconclusive. The SQL delivered by this ticket is verified correct, but the part that matters to the requester - being able to open and read Metabase question 634 - could not be checked from this session.

How it was validated: the MGH analytics layer was rebuilt from the shipped create_analytics_views.sql inside a disposable instance's own mgb-mgh schema, loaded with local-anesthetic administrations placed deliberately on the Eastern/UTC boundary.

Positive: last_feb_drop_deepdive.sql over 2026-01-01 to 2026-04-01 returned one row per administration with the three LAST rule columns, provider role, case ID and MRN, including an administration where no rule fired (all three columns empty) and one where the provider resolved through the fallback to the case's primary practitioner. An administration at Eastern 2026-03-31 22:00 was included and bucketed as March. Counts reconcile with the error-rate report over the same data.

Negative: administrations at Eastern 2025-12-31 15:00, Eastern 2025-12-31 22:00 and Eastern 2026-04-01 01:00 were all absent, and the error-rate report produced no December and no April bucket. Nine of nine expectations passed.

Red check: the pre-fix versions of the three modified reports were run verbatim against the same data. Both error-rate reports went red exactly as predicted - a spurious December bucket carrying the two Eastern-December administrations leaked into a January-to-March report, and the March bucket disappeared entirely. The cause reproduces directly: the old expression returned 2025-12-31 19:00 UTC for a 2026-01-01 Eastern start, ten hours early on both edges. The deepdive was separately flipped to the raw-UTC bound its own header warns about and went from nine passes to seven passes and two failures. Both flips were reverted and the shipped files re-run green.

What is still open:

- Whether question 634 can actually be opened and read - the last comment on this ticket says it could not be, from MGH.
- Whether card 634 holds this SQL. The card name does not match the filename, so the Metabase sync tool would create a second card rather than update it.
- Whether the deepdive answered the question about the February drop; no finding is recorded here.

Automation: there is no automated coverage of the analytics SQL at all today, which is why a ten-hour window shift went unnoticed. The proposal is a fixture harness that runs the shipped create_analytics_views.sql on a scratch schema and drives pass/fail from an expectations table, plus boundary and DST regressions for the three reports this ticket changed and rule-status and provider-fallback cases for the deepdive.
